hints: Focus on where the ester links break, look for the two C-O single bonds next to each C=O in this diester.
Remember alkaline hydrolysis is different from acid hydrolysis, the carboxylic acid part becomes a sodium salt while the alcohol part stays as an alcohol.
Split the molecule into three pieces, two carboxylate ends and one middle diol, then check which option keeps the middle as HO...OH and both ends as ONa salts.
walkthrough:
**Spot the two ester groups**

Great start, let's read the structure. On the left you have $\text{H-C(=O)-O-CH}_2-$ which is a methanoate ester. On the right you have $-\text{CH}_2\text{-O-C(=O)-CH}_3$ which is an ethanoate ester. The middle is a 3-carbon chain.

Starting diester:
$$\text{HCOOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OCOCH}_3$$

**Recall alkaline hydrolysis rule**

With hot aqueous $\text{NaOH}$, an ester gives a sodium carboxylate plus an alcohol, not a free carboxylic acid. This is because any acid formed is immediately neutralised by the base.

General rule:
$$\text{RCOOR' + NaOH} \rightarrow \text{RCOONa + R'OH}$$

**Apply to both ends**

Now split at both C-O ester bonds. The left acyl part $\text{HCO-}$ becomes sodium methanoate, $\text{HCOONa}$. The right acyl part $\text{CH}_3\text{CO-}$ becomes sodium ethanoate, $\text{CH}_3\text{COONa}$. The middle $\text{-OCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{O-}$ picks up H on each O to become propane-1,3-diol.

Products:
$$\text{HCOONa + HOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH + CH}_3\text{COONa}$$

**Check the alcohol does not change**

A common worry is that the diol will also react with NaOH to give ONa. It will not. Alcohols are very weak acids and are not deprotonated by aqueous $\text{NaOH}$ under these conditions, so the middle stays as HO...OH.

options.A: Shows two free carboxylic acids, methanoic acid and ethanoic acid, plus the diol. This is the result of acid hydrolysis with dilute HCl or H2SO4, not alkaline hydrolysis. With excess NaOH the acids would be neutralised to their sodium salts.
options.B: Keeps the acids as free acids but wrongly turns the diol into a disodium alkoxide. This is back to front. The acids react with NaOH, the neutral alcohol does not react to any significant extent with aqueous NaOH.
options.C: Correctly shows sodium methanoate, propane-1,3-diol, and sodium ethanoate. Both ester links are cleaved to give carboxylate salts, while the central diol is regenerated unchanged as HO-CH2-CH2-CH2-OH.
options.D: Correctly shows the two sodium carboxylates but incorrectly shows the diol as NaO-CH2-CH2-CH2-ONa. Students choosing this remember the NaOH but apply it to the alcohol too. Alcohols do not form stable salts with aqueous NaOH, only the carboxylic acid parts do.
